q22735.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must stop on the right and wait for the carriageway to be clear.

explain.short: The procession occupies the road. You pull over to the right and wait until the road is free again.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'fermarsi sulla destra' (stop on the right) is the correct behaviour, nothing is wrong here.

sceneParams.caption: Procession ahead: stop on the right and wait
lines: Procession crossing the road in town
Wait until the road is clear

q22736.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must avoid using the horn.

explain.short: Honking does not make the procession faster and only creates tension. You wait in silence.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'evitare di suonare' (avoid sounding) is right: the horn is not a tool to clear the road.

sceneParams.caption: No horn at a procession
lines: Procession on the road in town

q22737.en: When a driver comes across a procession in a built-up area, it is advisable to turn into a side street, if possible, as long as the manoeuvre can be done correctly.

explain.short: Taking another road is a good way to avoid waiting, but only if you can turn safely and correctly.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'purché' (as long as) sets the condition: the side road is fine only with a correct manoeuvre.

sceneParams.caption: Side road is fine if you can turn correctly
lines: Side road on the right: indicator
Turn only if the manoeuvre is safe

q22738.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, before passing they must make sure it has gone by completely.

explain.short: People at the end of a procession may still be crossing. You move only when the last person has passed.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'completamente' (completely) is the key word: not half, the whole procession.

sceneParams.caption: Go only after the whole procession has passed
lines: Watch the end of the group
Go only when all have passed

q22739.en: When a driver comes across a procession in a built-up area, it is advisable to avoid reversing if this obstructs the flow of traffic.

explain.short: Reversing in town traffic can block or hit the cars behind you. If it hinders traffic, do not do it.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'se ciò ostacola' (if this obstructs): reversing is the problem only when it blocks others.

sceneParams.caption: Don't reverse if it blocks the cars behind

q22740.en: When a driver comes across a procession in a built-up area, it is advisable not to make a U-turn if that would obstruct traffic.

explain.short: A U-turn (inversione di marcia: turning round to go back) across busy town traffic blocks others. If it hinders traffic, wait instead.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'qualora' (if / in case) limits the ban to when the U-turn gets in the way.

sceneParams.caption: No U-turn if it gets in the way of traffic

q22741.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must sound the horn discreetly to tell the procession to clear the road as soon as possible.

explain.short: You never use the horn to hurry a procession, not even softly. The procession has the road; you wait.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'discretamente' (discreetly) sounds polite, but any horn to hurry people is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: No horn, not even a soft one: just wait
lines: Procession on the road in town
Even a short honk is wrong
Stop on the right and wait

q22742.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must try to make their way by cutting through the procession, but with extreme care.

explain.short: Driving through a group of people is dangerous and not allowed. 'Extreme care' does not make it right.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'ma con estrema prudenza' (but with extreme care) tries to make a wrong action sound safe.

sceneParams.caption: Never drive through a procession
lines: Stop on the right and wait

q22743.en: When a driver comes across a procession in a built-up area, it is advisable to switch on the high beams to see better and avoid accidents.

explain.short: High beams (luci di profondità: full headlights) dazzle the people in the procession. They do not help here.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'luci di profondità' are the high beams: they blind people, they do not make you safer.

sceneParams.caption: No high beams: they dazzle the people

q22744.en: When a driver comes across a procession in a built-up area, if they are really in a hurry, it is advisable to pass quickly using the horn continuously.

explain.short: Being in a hurry never allows you to rush past people or to honk all the time. You stop and wait.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'se proprio ha molta fretta' (if really in a hurry): your hurry is never an excuse.

sceneParams.caption: In a hurry? Still stop and wait
lines: Procession on the road in town

q22745.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must act according to how dense it is, passing it or cutting through it whenever possible.

explain.short: Whether the procession is thick or thin, you never pass through it. You wait until it has gone.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'densità' (density) suggests a thin procession can be crossed; it cannot.

sceneParams.caption: Thick or thin: never cut through a procession

q22746.en: When, in a built-up area, a driver comes across a procession, they must reverse quickly to the first junction.

explain.short: Reversing quickly in town is dangerous for the cars and people behind you. You stop on the right and wait.
explain.rule: A procession (corteo) has the road for now: you stop on the right, stay calm and quiet, and wait until it has fully passed.
explain.trap: 'retrocedere rapidamente' (reverse quickly): fast reversing is a danger, not a duty.

sceneParams.caption: Don't reverse fast: stop on the right and wait
lines: Stop on the right and wait

q22747.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to wait patiently for it to move off.

explain.short: The driver ahead may have a problem or be distracted. A few seconds of patience keep everyone calm and safe.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'pazientemente' (patiently) is the right attitude, nothing is wrong here.

sceneParams.caption: Green light, car ahead slow: wait patiently
lines: Junction in town, light turns green
Car ahead does not move yet

q22748.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to avoid honking insistently and to avoid creating intolerance among other drivers.

explain.short: Honking again and again makes drivers nervous and angry. In towns the horn is only for immediate danger.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'evitare' (avoid) is right: insistent honking is what you must NOT do.

sceneParams.caption: No insistent honking: keep everyone calm
lines: Junction in town, car ahead slow

q22749.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable, if needed and if it can be done without danger, to help the driver who is stuck.

explain.short: The car may have broken down. Helping is good, but only when it is needed and safe for you and others.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'senza pericolo' (without danger) is the condition that makes helping correct.

sceneParams.caption: Car stuck at green: help if safe
lines: Car ahead stuck at the junction
Help only if needed and safe

q22750.en: In built-up areas it is forbidden to use the horn to urge the driver of the vehicle in front to move off when the traffic light turns green.

explain.short: In towns the horn (segnalatore acustico) may only be used for a real, immediate danger. Hurrying someone is not a danger.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'è vietato' (it is forbidden) is correct: in towns this use of the horn is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Town: no horn to hurry the car ahead
lines: Traffic light turns green in town

q22751.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, you must not overtake it with dangerous manoeuvres.

explain.short: Swerving around a slow car in a junction is risky for pedestrians and crossing traffic. Never do it in a dangerous way.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'non si deve' (you must not) is right: dangerous overtaking is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No risky overtaking at the junction
lines: Car ahead slow at the green light
No dangerous overtaking at the junction

q22752.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to honk insistently to urge the driver to move off.

explain.short: Insistent honking is rude and, in towns, the horn is only for immediate danger. You wait patiently.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'insistentemente' (insistently) is exactly the wrong behaviour.

sceneParams.caption: No insistent horn: wait patiently
lines: Car ahead slow at the green light

q22753.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to use the horn to get the attention of the drivers behind.

explain.short: There is no reason to honk at the cars behind. It only adds noise and stress; just wait.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'richiamare con il clacson' (call with the horn): the horn is not for this.

sceneParams.caption: No horn to call the drivers behind
lines: Car ahead slow at the green light
No horn for the cars behind

q22754.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to pull the handbrake and get out to look for a traffic officer who will take action.

explain.short: Leaving your car in the junction blocks traffic even more. A slow car is not a matter for the police.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'scendere' (get out of the car) makes the situation worse, not better.

sceneParams.caption: Don't get out looking for police: just wait
lines: Car ahead slow at the green light
Leaving your car blocks the junction
Stay in the car and wait

q22755.en: When, at a town junction, the vehicle in front is slow to move off at the green light, it is advisable to try to clear the road as quickly as possible, even by turning back.

explain.short: A U-turn at a busy junction is dangerous and blocks others. A slow car ahead is only a short wait.
explain.rule: Patience: no horn to hurry the driver (in towns the horn is only for immediate danger), no risky overtaking, help if needed.
explain.trap: 'anche invertendo il senso di marcia' (even by turning back) adds a dangerous U-turn.

sceneParams.caption: No U-turn at the junction: wait
lines: Car ahead slow at the green light

q22756.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must proceed carefully, using the dipped beams.

explain.short: Dipped beams (anabbaglianti: low headlights) do not blind the other driver. You go on with care because you see less.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'anabbaglianti' (dipped beams) is right: not the high beams.

sceneParams.caption: Oncoming high beams: dipped beams and care
lines: Night, oncoming car with high beams

q22757.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must look away from the beam of light so as not to be dazzled.

explain.short: Looking straight into strong lights blinds you for seconds. Look slightly to the right edge of the road.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'distogliere lo sguardo' (look away) is correct: towards the right edge, not into the lights.

sceneParams.caption: Look away to the right edge of the road
lines: Look at the right edge of the road

q22758.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must slow down suitably and stop if necessary.

explain.short: If you cannot see well, slow down. If you are really blinded, stopping safely is the right choice.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'eventualmente' (if necessary) means stop only when needed, not always.

sceneParams.caption: Dazzled: slow down, stop if needed
lines: Stop if you really can't see

q22759.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must take the reduced visibility into account in the way we drive.

explain.short: When you are dazzled you see less of the road. Your speed and moves must fit this.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'ridotta visibilità' (reduced visibility) is real, so your driving must adapt.

sceneParams.caption: Dazzled = you see less: drive for it
lines: You see less of the road

q22760.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must avoid sudden manoeuvres and lane changes.

explain.short: While you are dazzled you cannot see what is around you. A sudden swerve or lane change could hit someone.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'evitare' (avoid) is right: no sudden moves while you can't see well.

sceneParams.caption: Dazzled: no sudden moves, no lane changes

q22761.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must set the interior rear-view mirror to the anti-dazzle position.

explain.short: The anti-dazzle mirror position helps against lights from BEHIND. The car dazzling you here is in FRONT.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'retrovisore interno' (inside mirror) is for cars behind; 'incrociamo' means the car comes towards you.

sceneParams.caption: Anti-dazzle mirror is for lights from behind
lines: Dazzled by a car in front
Mirror only helps with lights behind
Look to the right edge, slow down

q22762.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must in turn drive with our high beams on, to see the road better.

explain.short: Then both drivers are blinded and the danger doubles. You use dipped beams.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'a nostra volta' (in turn) = answering back with high beams: never do this.

sceneParams.caption: Never answer with your own high beams

q22763.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must stop immediately.

explain.short: Stopping suddenly can cause a rear-end crash. You slow down and stop only if it is really needed.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'immediatamente' (immediately) is too strong: stop only if necessary.

sceneParams.caption: Not an immediate stop: slow down first
lines: Sudden stop: car behind may hit you
Slow down; stop only if needed

q22764.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must use the two-tone horns to get the attention of the oncoming vehicle.

explain.short: Two-tone horns (trombe bitonali) are not for this. At most you can flash your lights briefly; then you slow down.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'trombe bitonali' (two-tone horns) are not a way to warn a dazzling driver.

sceneParams.caption: No horns: dipped beams and slow down

q22765.en: When, at night on an out-of-town road, we meet a vehicle with its high beams on, we must try to shield our eyes with our hands.

explain.short: You need both hands on the steering wheel. Look away to the right edge instead.
explain.rule: Dazzled from the front: dipped beams, eyes to the right edge, slow down (stop if needed), no sudden moves.
explain.trap: 'con le mani' (with the hands): taking your hands off the wheel is dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Hands stay on the wheel: look away

q22766.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you must drive in a way suited to the features of the vehicle, the road and the traffic.

explain.short: A truck, a wet narrow road or heavy traffic all need a different way of driving. You adapt to all of them.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'adeguato' (suited) is the key: driving must fit the situation.

sceneParams.caption: Fit your driving to vehicle, road, traffic

q22767.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you must follow not only the traffic rules but also the precautions dictated by common sense.

explain.short: The rules cannot list every situation. Common sense fills the gaps and keeps you safe.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'non solo ... ma anche' (not only ... but also): rules AND common sense.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic rules + common sense

q22768.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you must combine applying the basic traffic rules with a strong civic sense.

explain.short: Civic sense (senso civico: respect for others and the community) makes you drive with care for everyone.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'unire' (combine): rules together with civic sense, both are needed.

sceneParams.caption: Traffic rules + respect for others

q22769.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you just need to respect the maximum speed limits.

explain.short: Speed limits are only one rule. You must also adapt to the road, the traffic and use common sense.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'limitarsi' (just / only) makes it false: speed limits alone are not enough.

sceneParams.caption: Speed limits alone are not enough
lines: But also adapt to road and traffic

q22770.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you must always drive at a constant speed.

explain.short: Speed must change with the road, bends, traffic and weather. Keeping it always the same can be dangerous.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) makes it false: speed must adapt.

sceneParams.caption: Speed must change with the situation
lines: Clear road: you can go faster

q22771.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you must in any case give way to all vehicles at junctions.

explain.short: Giving way to everybody confuses others and blocks traffic. You follow the priority rules and signs.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'comunque' and 'tutti' (in any case, all): you give way only when the rules say so.

sceneParams.caption: Give way only when the rules say so
lines: Giving way to everyone blocks traffic

q22772.en: To avoid being a danger or an obstruction to traffic, you just need to respect the minimum speed limits.

explain.short: Minimum limits are only one rule. You must also adapt to the vehicle, road and traffic, with common sense.
explain.rule: Rules alone are not enough: you adapt to your vehicle, the road and the traffic, and add common sense.
explain.trap: 'limitarsi' (just / only) makes it false: minimum limits alone are not enough.

sceneParams.caption: Minimum limits alone are not enough
lines: But also adapt to road and traffic

q22773.en: In heavy traffic the driver must adjust their speed, matching it as much as possible to that of the traffic flowing along the lane they are in.

explain.short: If you go much slower or faster than the cars in your lane, you create danger. Move with the flow.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'uniformandola' (matching it) to your lane's flow is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy traffic: match the speed of your lane
lines: Busy road, queue in your lane
Match the speed of your lane
No sudden speeding up or braking

q22774.en: In heavy traffic the driver must always keep the safe distance from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: In heavy traffic cars brake often and suddenly. The safe distance is what saves you from a rear-end crash.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is correct here: the safe distance is never optional.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy traffic: always keep the safe distance
lines: Time to brake if they stop

q22775.en: In heavy traffic the driver must avoid honking to urge the vehicles in front to go faster.

explain.short: The cars ahead cannot go faster in a queue. Honking only creates stress and is not allowed for this.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'evitare' (avoid) is right: the horn is not for hurrying others.

sceneParams.caption: No horn to hurry the cars ahead

q22776.en: In heavy traffic the driver must change lane repeatedly so as to always use the freest one.

explain.short: Jumping from lane to lane causes crashes and slows everyone down. Stay in your lane.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'ripetutamente' (repeatedly) is the wrong behaviour.

sceneParams.caption: Don't keep changing lanes in a queue
lines: Heavy traffic on a multi-lane road

q22777.en: In heavy traffic the driver must use the lanes reserved for public-service vehicles, if they are free.

explain.short: Reserved lanes (corsie riservate) are only for buses, taxis and other allowed vehicles, even when they are empty.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'se libere' (if free): an empty reserved lane is still forbidden for you.

sceneParams.caption: Bus lane: not for you, even if empty
lines: Lane reserved for buses and taxis

q22778.en: In heavy traffic the driver must use the simultaneous flashing of all direction indicators.

explain.short: Hazard lights (all indicators flashing) are not for normal heavy traffic. They are for real hazards, like a stopped car.
explain.rule: Heavy traffic: go with the flow of your lane, keep the safe distance, stay calm.
explain.trap: 'lampeggio simultaneo' (hazard lights): heavy traffic alone does not need them.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy traffic: no hazard lights needed

q22779.en: To turn right you must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: Staying close to the right edge stops anyone passing on your right and makes a short, safe turn.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'margine destro' (right edge) is correct for a right turn.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn: keep close to the right edge
lines: Keep close to the right edge

q22780.en: To turn right you must signal the manoeuvre in advance, using the direction indicator.

explain.short: Others must know what you will do before you do it. The indicator goes on in time, not at the last moment.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'in anticipo' (in advance) is key: signal early, not while turning.

sceneParams.caption: Indicator on in advance, then turn right

q22781.en: A right turn is made by moving into the lane that allows you to do this manoeuvre.

explain.short: When lanes are marked with arrows, you move early into the lane for turning right.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'corsia che consente' (the lane that allows) the right turn is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Use the lane marked for turning right
lines: Lanes with arrows before the junction
Move into the right-turn lane early

q22782.en: A right turn is made by reducing speed gradually as you approach the turning point.

explain.short: Slowing down gradually lets the cars behind react and lets you see pedestrians and bikes at the corner.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'man mano' (gradually) is correct: slow down step by step, not suddenly.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down gradually before the right turn

q22783.en: A right turn is made without creating danger or obstruction to others.

explain.short: Every manoeuvre, including a right turn, must be safe for pedestrians, bikes and other vehicles.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'senza creare pericolo o intralcio' (without danger or obstruction) is the general rule for every manoeuvre.

sceneParams.caption: Turn right only when it's safe for all

q22784.en: To turn right you must keep as close as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: For a right turn you keep to the RIGHT edge. The left edge would cross the path of other traffic.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'sinistro' (left) is swapped with 'destro' (right).

sceneParams.caption: Right turn = right edge, not left
lines: Stay close to the RIGHT edge

q22785.en: To turn right you must keep to the left lane.

explain.short: From the left lane you would cut across the cars on your right. You turn right from the right lane.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'corsia di sinistra' (left lane) is the wrong side for a right turn.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn from the right lane
lines: Turning right: use the right lane

q22786.en: A right turn is made without ever giving way to pedestrians, if the traffic light is green.

explain.short: With your green light, pedestrians may also have green on the road you turn into. You must give way to them.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'senza mai' (without ever): green does not cancel the pedestrians' priority.

sceneParams.caption: Green light: still give way to pedestrians

q22787.en: A right turn is made by going round the light column placed, if present, in the centre of the junction.

explain.short: Going round the centre is the way for some LEFT turns. For a right turn you stay at the right edge.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'girando attorno' (going round) the centre is not a right turn.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn: stay right, don't circle the centre
lines: Light column in the middle of the junction
Right turn: keep to the right edge

q22788.en: When you want to turn right you must move close to the centre of the junction.

explain.short: The centre of the junction is where you go for a LEFT turn. For a right turn you stay close to the right edge.
explain.rule: Turning right: indicator early, keep close to the right edge, slow down, give way to pedestrians crossing.
explain.trap: 'centro dell'incrocio' (centre) belongs to the left turn, not the right turn.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn: right edge, not the centre
lines: Keep close to the right edge

q22789.en: On a two-way road with three lanes, as in the figure, the centre lane must be used only for overtaking.

explain.short: The centre lane (B) is shared by both directions. You use it only to overtake, then go back to your right lane.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is accepted here: the centre lane is not for normal driving.

sceneParams.caption: Three lanes, two ways: centre lane only to overtake

q22789.reviewNote: The Code also lets you use the centre lane of a 3-lane two-way road to prepare a left turn; 'solo per il sorpasso' may be stricter than art. 143.

q22790.en: On a two-way road with two lanes, as in the figure, the left lane must be used only for overtaking.

explain.short: The left lane belongs to the oncoming traffic. You go there only briefly to overtake, then return right.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is correct: you never drive normally in the left lane here.

sceneParams.caption: Two lanes, two ways: left lane only to overtake

q22791.en: On main out-of-town roads, parking is allowed only in the special areas.

explain.short: On these fast roads (strade extraurbane principali) a parked car on the side would be dangerous. You park only in the marked areas.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'solo nelle apposite aree' (only in the special areas) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Main out-of-town road: park only in special areas
lines: Park only in the marked areas

q22792.en: On a road with two separate carriageways, as in the figure, you must use the right carriageway for normal driving and the left one for overtaking.

explain.short: The two carriageways (carreggiate) are for opposite directions. You overtake inside your own carriageway, using its left lane.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'quella di sinistra per il sorpasso': the left carriageway is the other direction, not an overtaking road.

sceneParams.caption: Left carriageway = other direction, not overtaking

q22793.en: On roads made of one carriageway with two lanes and two-way traffic, as in the figure, you may drive in parallel rows.

explain.short: With one lane per direction there is no room for two rows side by side. The left lane is for oncoming traffic.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'file parallele' (parallel rows) need two lanes in YOUR direction; here there is only one.

sceneParams.caption: One lane each way: no parallel rows

q22794.en: On roads with four separate carriageways, the central ones are reserved for overtaking.

explain.short: Each carriageway (carreggiata) is a road for normal driving in its own direction. You overtake inside the carriageway you are on.
explain.rule: Keep right. On a two-way road, the lanes towards the middle are only for overtaking; separate carriageways each carry one direction.
explain.trap: 'riservate al sorpasso' (reserved for overtaking): no carriageway is only for overtaking.

sceneParams.caption: No carriageway is just for overtaking
lines: Each one: normal driving, one direction

q22795.en: Anyone who wants to change lane must check that the lane they want to use is free ahead for a sufficient distance.

explain.short: If a car is close ahead in the new lane, you could hit it. The lane must be free in front for enough road.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'davanti' (ahead) is one of the two checks: ahead and behind.

sceneParams.caption: New lane free far enough ahead
lines: Multi-lane road, you want to move

q22796.en: Anyone who wants to change lane must check that the lane they want to use is free behind for a sufficient distance.

explain.short: A faster car may be coming in the new lane. Check the mirrors and blind spot so it is free behind too.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'dietro' (behind) is checked with the mirrors, and is just as important as ahead.

sceneParams.caption: Mirror: new lane free far enough behind

q22797.en: Anyone who wants to change lane to overtake must check that the vehicle in front has not signalled the start of the same manoeuvre.

explain.short: If the car ahead is about to overtake too, you would both pull out together. Wait until it has finished.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'stessa manovra' (same manoeuvre): the car ahead has priority to overtake first.

sceneParams.caption: Car ahead signalled to overtake: wait

q22798.en: Anyone who wants to change lane must signal the manoeuvre in advance, using the direction indicator.

explain.short: The indicator tells the others what you will do before you do it. Put it on in time, not at the last moment.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'in anticipo' (in advance) is the key: signal early.

sceneParams.caption: Indicator in advance, then change lane
lines: Then move into the new lane

q22799.en: Anyone who wants to change lane must not create obstruction or danger for those travelling in the lane they want to enter.

explain.short: The cars already in that lane come first. If your move would make them brake or swerve, do not do it.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'non deve creare' (must not create) is correct: their safety comes first.

sceneParams.caption: Don't make the cars in that lane brake
lines: Car already in the next lane
Your move must not make it brake

q22800.en: Anyone who wants to change lane must not use the direction indicator if the road is clear.

explain.short: You always signal a lane change, even on an empty road. Someone you have not seen may be there.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'non deve ... se la strada è libera' (must not if clear): the indicator is always required.

sceneParams.caption: Always use the indicator, even on an empty road
lines: Still check mirror and blind spot

q22801.en: Anyone who wants to change lane is obliged to signal the manoeuvre with the horn (horn or trumpets).

explain.short: Lane changes are signalled with the indicator, not with the horn. The horn is only for danger.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'avvisatore acustico' (horn) is the wrong tool: it is the indicator.

sceneParams.caption: Lane change: indicator, not horn
lines: The horn is not for this

q22802.en: Before changing lane you must make sure that the lanes are separated by a solid line.

explain.short: It is the opposite: a solid line (striscia continua) must not be crossed. You change lane across a dashed line.
explain.rule: Changing lane: mirror and look (ahead and behind), indicator in advance, then move only if nobody is put in danger.
explain.trap: 'striscia continua' (solid line) forbids changing lane; the dashed line allows it.

sceneParams.caption: Solid line: no crossing. Dashed: you may
lines: Dashed line: you may change lane

q22803.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must move towards the centre of the carriageway.

explain.short: Moving next to the centre line lets cars behind pass you on the right while you wait to turn.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'centro della carreggiata' (centre of the road) is right; not the left edge.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn on a two-way road: move to the centre
lines: Left indicator, move to the centre line
Cars behind can pass on your right

q22804.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must, as a rule, use the left area of the junction, like the vehicles in the figure, unless signs say otherwise.

explain.short: In the picture the cars turn before the centre point, passing to its left. This is the normal Italian left turn.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'di norma' (as a rule) and 'salvo diversa segnalazione' (unless signs say otherwise) make it correct.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn: pass left of the centre, don't circle it
lines: Cars turn before the centre point

q22805.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must go round the centre of the junction like vehicle H in the figure, if there is a roundabout sign.

explain.short: The blue roundabout signs (rotatoria) change the rule: you drive round the centre, like H, instead of cutting in front of it.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'se c'è il segnale di rotatoria' (if there is the roundabout sign) is the condition that makes it right.

sceneParams.caption: Roundabout sign: go round the centre, like H
lines: Blue roundabout signs at the junction
H goes round the centre point
No sign: turn in front of it

q22806.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must give way to vehicles coming from the right, unless signs say otherwise.

explain.short: The basic priority rule applies: give way to the right. Signs or traffic lights can change it.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'salvo diversa segnalazione' (unless signs say otherwise) keeps it correct.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn: give way to traffic from the right
lines: It goes first, then you turn left

q22807.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must move as far as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: On a two-way road the left edge is on the oncoming traffic's side. You move to the centre line only.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'margine sinistro' (left edge) is right only on a ONE-way road, not on a two-way road.

sceneParams.caption: Two-way road: centre line, not left edge

q22808.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must do the manoeuvre quickly, to avoid the vehicles coming from the right and from the left.

explain.short: Turning fast is dangerous. You slow down, give way where required and turn calmly.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'velocemente' (quickly): speed never replaces giving way.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn: slow and calm, not fast

keywords.it: provenienti da destra e da sinistra
keywords.en: coming from the right and from the left

q22809.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must always turn using the right side of the junction, like the vehicles in the figure.

explain.short: In the picture the cars go round the centre point. Without a roundabout sign you turn in front of the centre, in the left area.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) and 'lato destro' (right side): going round the centre is only for roundabouts.

sceneParams.caption: No roundabout sign: don't go round the centre
lines: These cars go round the centre
Correct: left area of the junction
Round the centre only with roundabout

q22810.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must give way to vehicles coming from the left, unless signs say otherwise.

explain.short: The basic rule is to give way to the RIGHT, not to the left.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'da sinistra' (from the left) is swapped with 'da destra' (from the right).

sceneParams.caption: Give way to the RIGHT, not the left
lines: Give way to vehicles from the right
Not to those from the left

q22811.en: On a two-way carriageway, to turn left you must sound the horn, to cross the junction more safely.

explain.short: A left turn is signalled with the indicator. The horn is not part of turning and is only for danger.
explain.rule: Two-way road, left turn: move to the centre line, give way to the right, turn in the left area of the junction (round the centre only with a roundabout sign).
explain.trap: 'suonare il clacson' (sound the horn) is not required to turn.

sceneParams.caption: Left turn: indicator, not horn
